rows.annotation: YedI-family integral inner membrane protein of unknown molecular function.
rows.evidence: Three query domain searches identify inner membrane protein YedI across 94–97% of the sequence; query topology predicts six transmembrane helices. The 97%-identical STRING homolog belongs to MutK/YedI COG2354. Homolog expression studies and moderate cofitness correlations do not establish molecular activity. No substrate-specific fitness measurements or biochemical characterization are supplied.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier B: named YedI-family assignments and close homologs support family-level annotation, but the experimental summaries report expression or nutritional phenotypes rather than direct biochemical characterization. Neighborhood, cofitness, and Fitness Browser locus descriptions do not resolve activity or substrate. ABC transporter, GGDEF signaling, and DNA repair assignments are unsupported by convergent gene-specific evidence; the consistent YedI domains and query membrane topology support retaining only the membrane-protein family designation.

Vca0930 is a GGDEF protein in the pathogenic Vibrio cholerae C1 biotype. Its transcription is positively regulated by quorum regulatory sRNAs (Qrr), which act in an inverse relationship with the HapR regulator to link quorum sensing with c-di-GMP levels.

[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 41.80
Homolog originates from: Corynebacterium glutamicum ATCC 13032
Evidence type: experimental
This gene encodes a putative membrane protein. A transposon insertion in this gene resulted in an alternative nutritional requirement for either proline or threonine.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 39.70
Homolog originates from: Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv
Evidence type: comparative
This gene is identified as an example of a natural inversion event in M. tuberculosis strain F1 relative to the H37Rv reference strain (Fig. 1c). Comparative analysis of its GC skew values shows that the ancestral allele has a positive GC skew, while the inverted allele in strain F1 possesses a negative GC skew (-0.014).
[[END SUMMARY]]

rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 36 (in 20 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 35 (19 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 39.7-97.0
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
